relevance_note: The cohort includes one identifiable TNFAIP3 carrier with clinical detail: Table 1 lists 'P22' with 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)' and 'Type 1 Diabetes'.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown, including the converted supplement (Tables S1-S4). Rows were built by hand in a short Python script (no automatic table transcription); a second script checked every span verbatim and every schema field. Scope: 26-patient IEI cohort; only P22 carries a TNFAIP3 variant ('TNFAIP3 (P22)'); the other 25 patients (other genes) get no rows. Unlabelled sentences about 'one patient with a TNFAIP3 mutation' / 'One patient harboring a heterozygous mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene' were attributed to P22 because the paper states P22 is the single TNFAIP3 patient. Contradictions: (1) sex of P22 is 'M' in Table 1 but 'F' in Tables S3 and S4; Table 1 sums to 16 males/10 females whereas the text says '15 males and 11 females' (matching S3), so sex is recorded as not reported. (2) Results list P22 (type 1 diabetes) and P4 (IBD) among the nine patients with microarray-elevated autoantibodies despite negative routine tests, while the Discussion says those nine 'exhibited no overt autoimmune symptoms'; the unnamed Discussion statement was not used to exclude anything. (3) Text uses both 'type 1 diabetes' and 'type I diabetes'. Other notes: the Table 1 mutation cell reads 'TNFAIP3:c.2152del(40m)Hypergly' (stray text, apparently a typesetting artifact); variant recorded as c.2152del, no transcript or protein printed. Age at last evaluation is the 'Age' column (4Y) of Table S3 (immunological tests). '#' and '$' flags in Tables S3/S4 and the '\-' symbols in Tables S1/S2 are not defined in any legend, so they were not used as evidence; routine-autoantibody negativity comes from the text. Autoantibodies checklist item set to observed from the antigen-microarray findings (research assay, >=3-fold over healthy controls) although routine clinical autoantibody tests were negative; both phenotypic rows emitted. Peptic ulcers excluded from the named group statement '3 patients (P3, P4 and P5) had peptic ulcers' (narrower item, so the GI checklist item stays not reported). The cohort-level phrase 'a spectrum of pathogenic mutations was identified' was not recorded as a variant-specific classification. The paper never uses the terms A20 haploinsufficiency or HA20 for P22.
